parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor)

plans.note: Liability limits typically sit immediately after the all-caps warranty disclaimer block (Article VIX / sec-p0109 through sec-p0116); check for a one-sided cap protecting Licensor only, exclusion of consequential damages, and whether carve-outs (confidentiality, IP indemnity, willful misconduct) exist. Sweep General Provisions for a survival or catch-all limitation.

No heading signals indemnity; look in Article X (confidentiality) and General Provisions for an embedded indemnity. Given the broad disclaimer of non-infringement warranties in sec-p0112, a Licensor IP indemnity may be absent entirely — confirm before marking missing, and check for any reverse indemnity running against us.

Restrictions on Licensee are most likely in Article II (License Grant and Restrictions) and in the combined Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation article; check FIELD OF USE and DERIVATIVE WORK definitions for indirect limits on the businesses or competing products we may build or buy.

The defined term 'Right of First Refusal' is the key hook — trace its operative clause (likely Article VIII or the General Provisions) to see whether it locks us to Licensor for future platform needs. Also check Article II for any sole-source or exclusive-use covenant.

Pricing appears as a fixed per-unit tier table (sec-p0059 to sec-p0063) with 'Supplemental Payments' defined; an MFN in either direction is unlikely. Only flag if a clause obliges us to extend Licensor our best terms — an MFN in our favour is not to be touched.

Article X is expressly headed 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION' — read for mutuality, duration, scope (employees vs. customers/introducing brokers) and whether a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out exists.

Term and termination likely live in Article VIII alongside the 'Initial Period' definition in Article I. Check whether Licensee has a convenience right and on what notice, whether early-exit fees or acceleration of Supplemental Payments apply, and whether Licensor holds a broader walk-away right.

'Initial Period' is defined in Article I; the renewal mechanic and any non-renewal notice window should follow in Article VIII. Confirm the notice period is not longer than ~60 days and note (without flagging) any absence of a renewal price-uplift cap.

Governing law, venue and any arbitration provision are almost certainly in Article XXIV General Provisions. New York is likely given the 575 Madison Avenue address and would be compliant; watch for mandatory arbitration or a foreign forum.

Assignment sits in General Provisions. Confirm we may assign to AFFILIATEs (term is defined) and to a successor by merger without Licensor consent, and that a change of control of Licensee is not a Licensor termination trigger.

Ownership language will be driven by the Article I definitions (LICENSED SOFTWARE, LICENSED TECHNOLOGY, DERIVATIVE WORK, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, MORAL RIGHTS) and the acknowledgements in Article II. Check for any assignment to Licensor of our data, feedback, configurations or derivative works; Licensor ownership of its own pre-existing software is acceptable.

Article II is the grant clause. Test three things: whether the grant is revocable at will, whether AFFILIATEs and third-party contractors/service bureaus may use the Platform, and whether FIELD OF USE narrows the grant below our actual introducing-broker operations.

Usage-verification rights in volume-tiered licences typically ride with the grant restrictions (Article II) or with the payment/reporting mechanics behind the Market Day tier table. Check notice, frequency, on-site scope and who bears cost.

Look for late-payment interest, minimum-shortfall true-ups or stipulated damages tied to the Supplemental Payments and the tier table. Do not flag any service credits or remedies running in our favour.

Article VIX is an all-caps WARRANTY DISCLAIMER expressly disclaiming merchantability, non-infringement and fitness, and stating that defects may not be corrected — likely a deviation absent an affirmative performance warranty with a repair/replace or refund remedy. Cross-check any maintenance/support obligations elsewhere before concluding no warranty exists.
No insurance heading appears in the outline; General Provisions is the only plausible home. Given Licensor hosts the trading Platform and touches our data, flag as missing if nothing is found.

The descending per-Market-Day tier table plus the defined 'Supplemental Payments' and 'Initial Period' suggest a volume or minimum-fee commitment. Determine whether any minimum is payable regardless of usage and whether an exit exists; a purely volume-discount table with no floor is compliant.

Check the termination article and General Provisions for post-termination obligations; the confidentiality article may only require return/destruction of Confidential Information, which does not satisfy the rule. Flag missing if there is no data return in usable format and no wind-down/transition assistance period.
